newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan discounter pays top price for Osaka JNR land.
newsitem.headline: Japan discounter pays top price for Osaka JNR land.

text.p: Tokyo-based consumer goods discounter Yodobashi Camera Co Ltd paid a premium on Monday to grab a piece of prime real estate to expand the chain's reach into western Japan, analysts said.
"The said price seems about 20 percent higher than what could have been appropriate," said Koichiro Saito, analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research.

Unlisted Yodobashi Camera, which sells cameras and electronics goods at a discount, bid for and won about 2.15 hectares of top-ranked land in front of Osaka's biggest railway station from the JNR Settlement Corp for 101 billion yen.
"We really want to expand our business in the west from here," said Sumio Kitazawa of Yodobashi's public relations office.
Other bidders for the land were groups led by top high-end retailers Mitsukoshi Ltd and Parco Co Ltd, both of which already have outlets in the Kansai area of western Japan.
"Yodobashi must have really wanted the land, since this will be their first shop in the west. There was a special factor working there," Saito said.
Analysts said bids placed by Mitsukoshi and Parco must have ranged between 70 billion and 80 billion yen.
They said Yodobashi's singular bullishness does not exactly signal a recovery in land prices in Osaka, the commercial centre of western Japan.
Japan's real estate market has stagnated since the collapse of the 1980s "bubble" economy, as financial firms are laden with problem loans for which land is being held as collateral.

Up next in the Osaka real estate stakes will be U.S. companies American Malls International Corp and Koll Real Estate Group, who plan to form a consortium with Japanese firms to bid for another batch of land there in June.
The two developers plan to build a Mega-mall complex with floor space of up to 300,000 square metres, making it Japan's largest shopping complex.

"Like the previous ones auctioned in Tokyo, the next land to be sold in Osaka is also located in a premier shopping district," said Junichi Shiomoto, analyst at Nomura Research Institute. "It's also a good sign for Japan's real estate market that foreign names are already up."
On Friday, Mitsubishi Corp bought another tract of land auctioned by JNR Settlement Corp in Tokyo at 183.9 billion yen, to build commercial, hotel and office buildings.

In early February, land in the prestigious Ginza district of Tokyo sold in another JNR Settlement Corp auction fetched 372.3 billion yen. The land was sold to three consortiums including a Singaporean and Hong Kong joint venture.
Yodobashi said it had not decided how to secure the 150 billion yen required for the total project.
"We are not worried about that. Our owner Terukazu Fujisawa is one of the richest men in Japan," Yodobashi's Kitazawa said.
Yodobashi had sales of about 220 billion yen in the year to January 1997, he said.
